Updated assessment using the April 2021 Beige Book:

- Policy stance: The FOMC maintained ZLB rates, ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases, and the AIT framework while characterizing inflation as “transitory,” keeping financial conditions highly accommodative.
- Beige Book insights (April 2021): National activity accelerated with notable gains in consumer spending and tourism; vaccinations boosted employment and optimism. Hiring strengthened most in manufacturing, construction, and leisure/hospitality, but labor supply remained constrained, particularly for low-wage/hourly workers. Firms reported rising input costs tied to supply chain disruptions and earlier winter weather, with partial pass-through to prices—consistent with the “transitory” inflation narrative.
- Credit conditions (SLOOS): Broad easing versus 2020—standards looser for residential real estate (including GSE-eligible) and HELOCs; consumer credit (cards, auto, other) and IG corporates eased, especially at large banks. Some residual tightness persists for lower-quality borrowers; foreign banks were less accommodative; select C&I policies tightened at some large banks.

Implications: Accommodative policy plus improving credit supply and stronger real-side activity point to a moderately positive outlook. Headwinds from labor shortages and supply bottlenecks temper—but do not outweigh—the improvement. Net tone is somewhat more positive than the prior SLOOS-only reading.
